title: Scots Pine: Ancient Scots Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: The only pine native to nearly all of Europe. Helsinki's grows 340 years old beside a Bronze Age burial cairn, one of three mapped so far.
intro: Scots pine is the plainest tree here and one of the toughest: the only pine native to nearly all of Europe, from Spain to Siberia, growing wherever the soil is too thin or sandy for anything grander. That toughness is what kept these three alive and worth the walk. Helsinki's grows on a rocky shore beside a Bronze Age burial cairn built around 2000 BC, itself around 340 years old and barely 10 metres tall, stunted by three centuries rooted in bare granite. Strasbourg's did the opposite with its lifetime: a bole the city's own register calls tortuous, twisting up into a crown flattened into a parasol, ivy climbing but never feeding on the bark. Vilnius protects its pine by name alone, a single tree on a wooded hillside above the Song Valley amphitheatre, with nothing else written down. Three cities, three ways of surviving on thin ground.
